card: Prevents bitcoind from abruptly crashing via std::terminate when block or undo writes fail due to storage errors such as a full disk. BlockManager now explicitly flushes buffered writers inside try-catch blocks to route write errors through standard node fatal-error shutdown, while BufferedWriter clears its pending byte offset before writing so the destructor does not trigger a second write failure during stack unwinding. The author observed repeated crash terminations on full 1 TB benchmark disks and provided a reproducer demonstrating that write failures now exit cleanly instead of aborting.
changed_since_previous: No functional changes to the implementation; includes test structure adjustments and co-authorship attribution.
evidence: The author notes: "my 1 TB benchmarking servers have recently been filling up, so I've been seeing these failures more often" (PR description)

PR description provides a reproduction script demonstrating bitcoind aborting on short write without the fix, and cleanly logging 'Failed to write genesis block' and exiting with status 1 with the fix
problem: When block or undo writes fail due to disk issues (such as a full filesystem), `AutoFile::write_buffer()` throws an exception. Because `BufferedWriter` relies on its destructor to flush pending bytes and C++ destructors are implicitly `noexcept`, write failures cause `std::terminate` to abort the process without clean error reporting. Simply calling `flush()` before destruction was previously unsafe because a failed flush left pending bytes in the buffer, causing the destructor to throw a second exception during stack unwinding.

risk.why: Modifies block and undo serialization error handling in node storage; improper error handling could silently fail to persist blocks or bypass fatal shutdown on disk errors.

summary: Resets the pending byte count before calling the underlying write in `BufferedWriter::flush()` to avoid re-attempting writes during exception unwinding. Explicitly flushes the buffered writers in `BlockManager::WriteBlock` and `BlockManager::WriteBlockUndo` inside try-catch blocks so disk write failures trigger normal storage error handling and clean node shutdown rather than terminating the process.
